Ph.D. Program at the Faculty of Computer Science
Ph.D. Program at the Faculty of Computer Science
Copyright: © Kurt Beyer
This page contains all the key information on the doctoral programme – from the initial orientation to the final examination process.
At the Faculty of Computer Science, you will generally undertake your PhD as part of a research post. The research areas allocate PhD topics independently. Please refer to the websites of the individual chairs or our overview of research groups for current vacancies and research priorities.
A structured guide takes you step by step through the entire PhD process at the faculty – from the preparatory stages right through to the award ceremony:
Initial phase (Steps 1: Supervision agreement & 2: Admission): At the start of your PhD, you enter into a supervision agreement with your primary supervisor and then apply for admission to the PhD programme.
Examination phase (Steps 3: Examiners, 4: Examination & 5: Examination board): Shortly before completing your PhD, you nominate the additional examiners, submit your thesis for approval and have the examination board appointed.
Completion & Publication (Step 6): Following a successful examination, you will publish your doctoral thesis via the RWTH University Library. Upon completion of this step, you are entitled to use the doctoral title and will receive your doctoral certificate.
All applications relating to the doctoral programme must be submitted digitally via the Paperless platform.
For further details and the legal framework, please refer to the Doctoral Regulations of the Faculty of Computer Science. The Doctoral Office is available at all times as your central point of contact for any organisational queries regarding the process.
Admission requirements
To be admitted to doctoral studies at the Faculty of Computer Science, one of the following requirements must be met:
a degree in a relevant computer science-related field of study with a standard duration of at least eight semesters, for which a degree other than a bachelor's degree is awarded, or
a degree in a relevant, computer science-related field of study with a standard period of study of at least six semesters, as well as appropriate, preparatory studies in the doctoral subjects, or
Completion of a master's degree program within the meaning of § 61 Abs. 2 Satz 2 HG.
Step 1: Supervision Agreement
Before admission to the PhD programme can be granted, a supervision agreement with a professor of computer science is required.
Step 2: Admission to PhD
Required documents
The following documents are required for the application for admission to a PhD programme:
Supervision agreement: The signed agreement from Step 1.
University entrance qualification: e.g. A-level certificate.
Curriculum vitae in tabular form: Required if your degree was not obtained in Computer Science at RWTH.
Proof of degree: Proof of a relevant degree. Note: If you have successfully completed a Master’s degree at RWTH in Computer Science, Data Science, Software Systems Engineering or Media Informatics, this separate proof is not required.
Certificate of good conduct: In accordance with the Doctoral Regulations (§ 22(1d)), proof that you have no final conviction is required for admission. This proof may be provided either by a valid employment contract in the public sector (e.g. at RWTH) or by a certificate of good conduct for official purposes (document type O).
Please arrange for the relevant authority (e.g. the City of Aachen) to send the document directly to the Doctoral Office of the Faculty of Computer Science.
ubmitting an application via Paperless
Applications are submitted digitally via the Paperless portal. Depending on your current status at RWTH, please use one of the following methods:
Using RWTH Single Sign-On (SSO): Log in directly using your usual RWTH login details. If you do not already have one, first create the profile ‘Computer Science (PhD)’ – if you do not have a student ID number, use the placeholder 123456. If the application for your chosen degree programme is not displayed immediately, please use the option ‘Submit an application for another degree programme’.
Without RWTH access (local account): First, create a local account in Paperless. Enter your contact details and select the programme profile “Computer Science (PhD)” (placeholder student number: 123456), then start the application process.
Processing of the application for admission to a PhD programme
Once the application has been submitted via Paperless, it will be processed by the PhD Office. Depending on the type of application, processing may take up to two weeks. For applications where the university entrance qualification and/or the degree used for admission to the PhD programme was obtained abroad, processing may take longer. In such cases, other departments must verify the university entrance qualification and, where necessary, conditions for the doctoral programme may be set. You will then receive notification of your admission to the doctoral programme via Paperless. With this notification, you can enrol on the doctoral programme at RWTH.
The research phase: your PhD thesis & qualification
Once you have been admitted, you will devote yourself to independent academic work on your research topic and compile the findings for your doctoral thesis. During this key period of study and research, you will not only receive academic supervision from your department, but will also be provided with targeted support through the RWTH’s
Center for Young Academics
. Through tailored professional development programmes, mentoring and networking opportunities, the Centre provides you with personalised support for your academic development and career planning.
Step 3: Appointment of the second/third reviewers
Having appointed your primary supervisor in the first step, in this phase you should apply for assessment by additional examiners via the Paperless portal.
Deadline, requirements & supporting documents
Application deadline: Please note that the application to appoint the examination board should be submitted at least 3 weeks before the planned date, as the necessary documents must be prepared and the prescribed deadlines for sending invitations must be met. If you are planning a short-notice appointment, please contact the Doctoral Office in advance by email or telephone.
Consultation: Please agree on the selection of the second (and, if applicable, third) reviewer with your primary supervisor before submitting your application.
Qualifications: Reviewers must generally hold a professorship, honorary professorship or private lecturer position at a university or non-university research institution in Germany or abroad.
Voting rights in the faculty: At least one reviewer must have voting rights in the Faculty of Computer Science (this is usually covered by the first reviewer). Should this not be the case, a third reviewer must be appointed.
Declaration of Conflict of Interest: The application must be accompanied by a signed Declaration of Conflict of Interest from the second or third reviewer.
Processing and Feedback
Once submitted via Paperless, your application will be processed by the Doctoral Office. The review period usually takes up to two weeks. Once the process is complete, you will receive notification of the official appointment of the examiners directly via Paperless.
Step 4: Admission to the PhD examination
By submitting your application for admission to the doctoral examination, you are initiating the assessment process for your doctoral thesis.
Required documents
The following documents are required for your application:
Doctoral thesis: The finalised thesis to be assessed.
Certificate of ‘Good Academic Practice’: Proof of successful completion of the course ‘Good Academic Practice’ or, alternatively, ‘Academic Integrity’.
Note: If you have already completed this as part of a Master’s programme at RWTH, no further proof is required.
Proof of no criminal convictions: As in Step 2, either a valid employment contract in the public sector (e.g. at RWTH) or a certificate of good conduct for official purposes (document type O), sent directly to the Doctoral Office of the Faculty of Computer Science.
Procedure and Deadlines
Submitting your application via Paperless: Submit your application for admission to the doctoral examination digitally via Paperless. Following the examination, you will receive notification of whether your application has been accepted or rejected via the same platform.
Review period (3 months): In parallel with the admission process, the examiners are asked to submit their reports to the Doctoral Office within three months.
Publication period (2 weeks): As soon as all reports have been received, the Doctoral Office will inform you of the start of the publication period.
Tip on time management: Use the two-week publication period to prepare for the doctoral examination, agree on the venue and time, and finalise the composition of the examination board.
Step 5: Ordering the Commission
In this step, you will coordinate the organisational arrangements for the public lecture (advanced seminar) and for the subsequent closed-door oral examination, and apply for the official appointment of the examination board.
Composition of the examination board
The examination board consists of 4 (in exceptional cases, 5) members:
First and second examiners: Must hold a professorship, honorary professorship or private lecturership at a university or non-university research institution. At least one of these two individuals must have voting rights within the Faculty of Computer Science (usually the first supervisor; otherwise, a third examiner with voting rights within the faculty must be appointed).
Chair: A person authorised to conduct examinations from the Department of Computer Science at RWTH.
Subject examiner: A person authorised to conduct examinations from the Department of Computer Science at RWTH.
Note: The subject to be examined must be a computer science course offered by RWTH; it must not be too closely related to the topic of the doctoral thesis and must not be taught by one of the examiners.
Procedure & Organisation
Agreeing on the date and venue: Please agree on the date and venue for the advanced seminar and the subsequent oral examination in advance.
Note on room booking: If you wish to use the faculty’s rooms in E3 for the advanced seminar and/or the examination, you can request these by email.
Submitting the application via Paperless: Submit the application to appoint the examination board digitally via Paperless.
Official examination invitation:
- The Doctoral Office will send the invitation to the members of the examination board and to the deans’ offices of other faculties by email.
- You are responsible for sending out the invitation to the public seminar yourself. To do this, draw up an announcement based on the template and send it by email to the following distribution list: research assistants, professors, lecturers, secretariats, the webteam and the library.
Note on publication: Upon receipt of your email, the faculty’s web team will publish the announcement on the faculty website as soon as possible.
Step 6: Publication & Receipt of Certificate
The final step involves the publication of your thesis via the RWTH Aachen University Library and the formal award of your doctoral degree.
Publication via the University Library
A printed and hardbound copy of your thesis is required for publication.
Formatting: The title page must conform exactly to the template provided by the Faculty of Computer Science. As an alternative to the PDF, you may also create the title page yourself (e.g. using LaTeX), provided it matches the template visually. You may also include your own title page in your published thesis in addition to this one.
Affidavit: This may optionally form part of the bound thesis.
Important documents: Please remember to submit the author’s agreement and to register via RWTH Publicationa.
Recommendation from the Library: Please contact the UB by email well in advance of your final submission. This will help you avoid unnecessary corrections later on. Detailed information can be found on the University Library’s information page on online publication.
Completion of the procedure & use of the title
Acknowledgement of receipt: Once your thesis has been submitted, the library will send your copy, together with an acknowledgement of receipt, to the Doctoral Office for confirmation. Following a further review, the thesis will be published. You will receive an email notification of this from the library.
Use of the doctoral title: As soon as publication has been officially completed by the library, you are entitled to use the title Dr. rer. nat. or Dr.-Ing.
Issue of the certificate: Your doctoral certificate will then be prepared. You will be informed by email as soon as the document is ready, and you can choose whether to collect the certificate in person or have it sent by post.
Good luck with your PhD!
The Faculty of Computer Science is delighted to support you on your journey towards a PhD and wishes you every success in your research, your upcoming examinations and your personal and professional future!
